redcap_row.comments_v2: Prompt role assignment following EMS handoff (01:02). High-quality chest compressions started at 01:20 with minimal peri-check pauses (4s pause at 03:52 and 4s pause at 06:06; chest compression fraction ~98.1%). PEA was immediately recognized as non-shockable (01:22). Epinephrine 1 mg IV was administered promptly at 01:44 and repeated at 04:03. LMA/advanced airway was placed at 01:50 and confirmed via bilateral lung auscultation at 03:24. H's and T's (hypoxia, pulmonary embolism, electrolyte derangement/hypovolemia from diarrhea, acidosis, hypoglycemia) were systematically reviewed. ROSC was achieved at 06:09 with appropriate post-arrest care (IV fluids, 12-lead ECG, chest X-ray, head CT, and specialist consultations).
redcap_row.feedback_narrative_v2:
1. Immediate Recognition & High-Quality CPR: Following EMS handoff at 01:02, the Team Leader rapidly assigned roles and initiated chest compressions at 01:20. The team maintained continuous compressions with a 98.1% compression fraction and ultra-short 4-second pauses for pulse/rhythm checks at 03:52 and 06:06.
2. ACLS Non-Shockable Algorithm Adherence: The Team Leader explicitly verbalized at 01:22 that PEA is a non-shockable rhythm and prioritized early epinephrine (1st dose at 01:44, 2nd dose at 04:03) and airway placement (01:50).
3. Opportunities for Improvement: While airway placement was verbalized at 01:50, auscultation of bilateral breath sounds to confirm placement was delayed until 03:17–03:24 (87 seconds later). Additionally, sodium bicarbonate was suggested twice (04:06 and 05:51) without a closed-loop order or confirmation of administration, and compressor switching was not performed at the 2-minute mark.
redcap_row.general_comments_v2: The Team Leader maintained a calm, composed demeanor and regularly solicited input from the team ('does anybody have any other suggestions?' at 03:09, 05:49). Closed-loop communication was strong for epinephrine administration (01:44, 04:03) and lung auscultation (03:17), though ancillary medication suggestions (sodium bicarbonate at 04:06, 05:51) were floated without direct assignment or confirmation.
redcap_row.other_med_considered_list_v2: Sodium Bicarbonate, Nebulized bronchodilator (COPD), IV Fluids (post-ROSC)

utterances.text: EMS, I'm also your facilitator. Uh some disbelief will be suspended. When I ask you guys to intubate with the LMA, um just bag or say verbalize bagging, and when you're giving meds, verbalize the meds.

So, this man is uh 57 or this woman is a 57-year-old woman who has emphysema and is on oxygen at home. Her family states that the patient has been ill with nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea for several days. In the past 48 hours, she has been unable to eat or drink anything. Today she had more trouble breathing than usual, and her breathing has gradually worsened. She was found by EMS unresponsive and cyanotic at home. Um we found her in a hospital-type bed, and she appeared to be non-responsive. We started CPR, and we placed an IV. Um her initial vitals: she had a uh heart rate of 116, respiratory rate of zero, there was no pulse, um no oxygen, and her heart rhythm was sinus tachycardia with PEA. Um and yes, please assign yourself roles and and begin.
You like compressions or airway? Okay, you can do compressions, I'll do airway. Meds? And I will be the provider.
So compressions. Start compressions.

So we knew she was in PEA when she came in. Um we don't have an airway, so we want to get an airway. Um she's currently in PEA still, so we can't shock. Um we need to push one of epinephrine while we're getting the airway.
So I'm going to give meds, one milligram of epinephrine.
Okay, so one of epi's given. We have our airway, we're currently bagging, we're doing CPR. Um airway's in.

Um so we know that she was found unresponsive. She has a history of what, was it emphysema? Um she wears oxygen at home we know about. Um she's in PEA so we can rule out other things that we think's happening. Um as far as like H's and T's, she could be hypoxic, um she could have any type of like clot or thrombus with her um emphysema breathing history, like a PE. Um I don't know if we got labs or anything else yet. Does she have a cardiac history?
That she was having diarrhea before.

Okay, so that makes sense for electrolyte derangements. Um we knew it was PEA, it's probably we'll say two minutes, we can do a pulse check, we already pushed one of epinephrine. Um does anybody have any other suggestions?
Um if we could listen to lung sounds to confirm placement.
All right, listening.
You hear bilateral breath sounds.
Okay, tube is in, we're bagging. Um we can say it's about two minutes, so let's do a pulse check and see where the rhythm's at. Does she have a pulse?
You do not feel a pulse.
Okay, so continue compressions, she's still in PEA. Um we can give another push of epinephrine.
Gave epinephrine.
Um we can give sodium bicarbonate.
Uh could we get a point-of-care glucose? Do we have labs back?
We don't have labs back, but your uh point-of-care glucose is within normal range.
We can do like CBC, CMP, um I would do a troponin, um VBG, lactate, or just do an ABG and just see what her oxygen status was before, um do a D-dimer, sounds like possibility of a PE. Is family here?
No, family is not here.
Could do an amp of sodium bicarbonate, I'm sure she's got like some acidosis going on. Um it's about two minutes, we can check a pulse again. Do we have a pulse?
You guys have a pulse. Um so now her repeat vitals are she is tachycardic to 110, blood pressure is 95 over 77, respiratory rate's 14, SpO2 is 94, and her PCO2 is 40.
So do we know what rhythm she's in? Normal sinus. Okay. Give fluids, she's dehydrated most likely.

Is she like conscious right now? No, she's still unconscious. Okay. Pulm, cardiology should be consulted. Um we're still waiting for blood work, I would get an EKG, CT head to rule out strokes, chest X-ray to confirm the ET tube and everything.
All right guys, this ends your sim. Thank you.

done_well.title: Immediate PEA Recognition, Early Epinephrine, and 98.1% Chest Compression Fraction
done_well.detail: At 01:20, chest compressions were initiated immediately after role assignment. At 01:22, the Team Leader explicitly confirmed PEA as a non-shockable rhythm and ordered 1 mg epinephrine (administered at 01:44, repeated at 04:03). Pulse checks at 03:52 and 06:06 took only 4 seconds each.
done_well.evidence_quote: she's currently in PEA still, so we can't shock. Um we need to push one of epi while we're getting the airway.

done_well.title: Thorough Verbalization of Reversible Causes & Targeted Workup
done_well.detail: Between 01:59 and 04:55, the team collaboratively reviewed hypoxia, pulmonary embolism/thrombosis, hypovolemia and electrolyte derangements secondary to several days of vomiting/diarrhea, hypoglycemia (POC glucose checked at 04:10), and acidosis.
done_well.evidence_quote: as far as like H's and T's, she could be hypoxic, um she could have any type of like clot or thrombus... That she was having diarrhea before. Okay, so that makes sense for electrolyte derangements.

done_well.title: Structured Post-ROSC Stabilization and Diagnostic Bundle
done_well.detail: Upon achieving ROSC at 06:09, the team immediately assessed rhythm and vitals, ordered IV fluids for dehydration/borderline hypotension (95/77 mmHg), assessed neurological responsiveness, and ordered a 12-lead ECG, chest X-ray, head CT, and Pulmonology/Cardiology consults.
done_well.evidence_quote: Give fluids, she's dehydrated most likely... Pulm, cardiology should be consulted... I would get an EKG, CT head to rule out strokes, chest X-ray to confirm the ET tube.

areas_for_improvement.title: 87-Second Delay Between Airway Placement and Auscultation Confirmation
areas_for_improvement.detail: The airway was reported in place with bagging at 01:50, but bilateral breath sounds were not auscultated to confirm placement until the Airway MD prompted it at 03:11 (confirmed at 03:24).
areas_for_improvement.actionable_recommendation: Immediately upon inserting an advanced airway or supraglottic device, perform primary confirmation (bilateral chest rise and 5-point auscultation) and secondary confirmation (continuous waveform capnography).
areas_for_improvement.evidence_quote: Um if we could listen to lung sounds to confirm placement. / You hear bilateral breath sounds.

areas_for_improvement.title: Unconfirmed Suggestions for Sodium Bicarbonate
areas_for_improvement.detail: The Team Leader mused 'we can give bicarb' at 04:06 and 'could do an amp of bicarb' at 05:51, but never issued a direct order to the Medication Nurse, resulting in no confirmation or administration.
areas_for_improvement.actionable_recommendation: Separate clinical brainstorming from medication orders: when deciding to give a medication, address the Medication Nurse by name/role with a specific dose and route, and require a closed-loop verbal read-back.
areas_for_improvement.evidence_quote: Could do an amp of bicarb, I'm sure she's got like some acidosis going on.

areas_for_improvement.title: Single Compressor Maintained Throughout Entire Arrest (~4 min 46 sec)
areas_for_improvement.detail: The same team member performed chest compressions continuously from 01:20 to ROSC at 06:06 without rotating compressors during the 2-minute rhythm check at 03:52.
areas_for_improvement.actionable_recommendation: Rotate compressors every 2 minutes during scheduled rhythm/pulse checks to prevent rescuer fatigue and preserve chest compression depth and recoil.
areas_for_improvement.evidence_quote: Okay, so continue compressions, she's still in PEA.

engine_team_review.team_narrative: The Team Leader maintained a calm, composed demeanor and regularly solicited input from the team ('does anybody have any other suggestions?' at 03:09, 05:49). Closed-loop communication was strong for epinephrine administration (01:44, 04:03) and lung auscultation (03:17), though ancillary medication suggestions (sodium bicarbonate at 04:06, 05:51) were floated without direct assignment or confirmation.
engine_team_review.technical_narrative: Prompt role assignment following EMS handoff (01:02). High-quality chest compressions started at 01:20 with minimal peri-check pauses (4s pause at 03:52 and 4s pause at 06:06; chest compression fraction ~98.1%). PEA was immediately recognized as non-shockable (01:22). Epinephrine 1 mg IV was administered promptly at 01:44 and repeated at 04:03. LMA/advanced airway was placed at 01:50 and confirmed via bilateral lung auscultation at 03:24. H's and T's (hypoxia, pulmonary embolism, electrolyte derangement/hypovolemia from diarrhea, acidosis, hypoglycemia) were systematically reviewed. ROSC was achieved at 06:09 with appropriate post-arrest care (IV fluids, 12-lead ECG, chest X-ray, head CT, and specialist consultations).
engine_team_review.feedback_narrative:
1. Immediate Recognition & High-Quality CPR: Following EMS handoff at 01:02, the Team Leader rapidly assigned roles and initiated chest compressions at 01:20. The team maintained continuous compressions with a 98.1% compression fraction and ultra-short 4-second pauses for pulse/rhythm checks at 03:52 and 06:06.
2. ACLS Non-Shockable Algorithm Adherence: The Team Leader explicitly verbalized at 01:22 that PEA is a non-shockable rhythm and prioritized early epinephrine (1st dose at 01:44, 2nd dose at 04:03) and airway placement (01:50).
3. Opportunities for Improvement: While airway placement was verbalized at 01:50, auscultation of bilateral breath sounds to confirm placement was delayed until 03:17–03:24 (87 seconds later). Additionally, sodium bicarbonate was suggested twice (04:06 and 05:51) without a closed-loop order or confirmation of administration, and compressor switching was not performed at the 2-minute mark.

done_well.title: Immediate PEA Recognition, Early Epinephrine, and 98.1% Chest Compression Fraction
done_well.detail: At 01:20, chest compressions were initiated immediately after role assignment. At 01:22, the Team Leader explicitly confirmed PEA as a non-shockable rhythm and ordered 1 mg epinephrine (administered at 01:44, repeated at 04:03). Pulse checks at 03:52 and 06:06 took only 4 seconds each.
done_well.evidence_quote: she's currently in PEA still, so we can't shock. Um we need to push one of epi while we're getting the airway.

done_well.title: Thorough Verbalization of Reversible Causes & Targeted Workup
done_well.detail: Between 01:59 and 04:55, the team collaboratively reviewed hypoxia, pulmonary embolism/thrombosis, hypovolemia and electrolyte derangements secondary to several days of vomiting/diarrhea, hypoglycemia (POC glucose checked at 04:10), and acidosis.
done_well.evidence_quote: as far as like H's and T's, she could be hypoxic, um she could have any type of like clot or thrombus... That she was having diarrhea before. Okay, so that makes sense for electrolyte derangements.

done_well.title: Structured Post-ROSC Stabilization and Diagnostic Bundle
done_well.detail: Upon achieving ROSC at 06:09, the team immediately assessed rhythm and vitals, ordered IV fluids for dehydration/borderline hypotension (95/77 mmHg), assessed neurological responsiveness, and ordered a 12-lead ECG, chest X-ray, head CT, and Pulmonology/Cardiology consults.
done_well.evidence_quote: Give fluids, she's dehydrated most likely... Pulm, cardiology should be consulted... I would get an EKG, CT head to rule out strokes, chest X-ray to confirm the ET tube.

areas_for_improvement.title: 87-Second Delay Between Airway Placement and Auscultation Confirmation
areas_for_improvement.detail: The airway was reported in place with bagging at 01:50, but bilateral breath sounds were not auscultated to confirm placement until the Airway MD prompted it at 03:11 (confirmed at 03:24).
areas_for_improvement.actionable_recommendation: Immediately upon inserting an advanced airway or supraglottic device, perform primary confirmation (bilateral chest rise and 5-point auscultation) and secondary confirmation (continuous waveform capnography).
areas_for_improvement.evidence_quote: Um if we could listen to lung sounds to confirm placement. / You hear bilateral breath sounds.

areas_for_improvement.title: Unconfirmed Suggestions for Sodium Bicarbonate
areas_for_improvement.detail: The Team Leader mused 'we can give bicarb' at 04:06 and 'could do an amp of bicarb' at 05:51, but never issued a direct order to the Medication Nurse, resulting in no confirmation or administration.
areas_for_improvement.actionable_recommendation: Separate clinical brainstorming from medication orders: when deciding to give a medication, address the Medication Nurse by name/role with a specific dose and route, and require a closed-loop verbal read-back.
areas_for_improvement.evidence_quote: Could do an amp of bicarb, I'm sure she's got like some acidosis going on.

areas_for_improvement.title: Single Compressor Maintained Throughout Entire Arrest (~4 min 46 sec)
areas_for_improvement.detail: The same team member performed chest compressions continuously from 01:20 to ROSC at 06:06 without rotating compressors during the 2-minute rhythm check at 03:52.
areas_for_improvement.actionable_recommendation: Rotate compressors every 2 minutes during scheduled rhythm/pulse checks to prevent rescuer fatigue and preserve chest compression depth and recoil.
areas_for_improvement.evidence_quote: Okay, so continue compressions, she's still in PEA.

engine_team_review.human_reviewer: Test Research Team / Trial Run Tabby and Sarah
engine_team_review.human_feedback_narrative: verbalized reversible causes of cardiac pea arrest, gave appropriate meds, no closed loop communication regarding admin of bicarb etc so I could not tell if it was actually given, appreciated leader asking for opinions, consider switching out for compressions and delegating differently
engine_team_review.human_team_comments: Could improve in closed loop communication particularly around administration of meds, it was not clear if certain meds were administered or not. They did do a good job of collaborating mentally, they had clear defined roles and were calm and organized.
